grades.quote: Reads and writes of I/O devices may have visible side effects, but accesses to main memory cannot.
grades.reason: The passage covers part of the question. It separates main memory from I/O device regions in a RISC-V hart's address space, and it says I/O accesses can have visible side effects while main memory accesses cannot. It also says implicit reads of side-effect-free memory may be done speculatively and cached. It does not name explicit cacheability attributes, such as PMAs, that would fully answer the question.
